questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Amplitude-Phase Form for Cosine
questions.worked_solution:
The difference formula for cosine gives  

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡(8x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(8x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(8x)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(8x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(8x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(8x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=1 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=1\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =1 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =1 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\ ϕ & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={1}^{2}+{1}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =2 \\ {R}^{2} & =2 \\ R & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(8x)=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x-\frac{\pi }{4})
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the expression $2(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$

$ϕ=$ 
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\ ϕ & =60\,{\,}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the expression $\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$

$ϕ=$ 
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$

The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{6} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ ϕ & =arctan\,(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\ ϕ & =30\,{\,}^{∘}.\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Amplitude-Phase Form for Sine
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=3 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={3}^{2}+(3\sqrt{3})^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =9+27 \\ {R}^{2} & =36 \\ R & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=6\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x+{60}^{∘})
$$
